content.text: No liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination fee payable by Corio appear anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee-on-termination or early-termination charge payable by Corio (the customer/licensee). Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", "interest" and "minimum" return no such mechanic; the Fees section (4.1-4.4) and Exhibit B payment terms impose only accrued license, maintenance, MarketSite access, implementation and revenue-share amounts, and Section 11 permits termination for uncured material breach or insolvency without any pre-agreed damages sum. Section 11.3 only preserves ordinary payment obligations for Customers Corio continues to serve, which is a survival of accrued fees rather than a liquidated amount. The revenue-share and support commitments in Exhibits B and C run in Corio's favour, and Corio's remedies for non-acceptance or warranty breach (refund of prepaid fees under 3.x, 7 and 8) benefit us, so they are not flagged. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer); no redline is required.
